turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Hi, this is Ethan calling from Acme Life. I'm returning a call-back request about our term life coverage. Am I speaking with Ava?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, that's me. I filled out the form on your ad the other night. I've got maybe ten minutes before I need to get back to the shop, so if we can keep it quick, that'd be great.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Absolutely, I'll keep it moving. Before we get into any details, could you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Ava Louise MacDonald, March 14th, 1988.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Ava, that matches what I have. So, Acme Term Life is straightforward life insurance. You pick a coverage amount and a term, and if you pass away during that term, your beneficiaries get a tax-free lump sum. Before I suggest anything, can I ask what got you thinking about coverage?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Honestly? I just signed a new five-year lease on a bigger space for my bakery, and I've got a line of credit tied to it. Plus my partner and I have a four-year-old. If something happened to me, I don't want them stuck with all of it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That makes total sense. Roughly how much are we talking between the line of credit and anything else you'd want covered, like the mortgage or childcare?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: The line of credit's about eighty thousand. Mortgage is around two hundred and forty, but my partner's on that too and has some coverage through work. I'd mostly want the business debt gone and a cushion for our daughter.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. And are you thinking short term, just while the business debt's there, or longer, say until your daughter's grown?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Longer, I guess. Until she's out of school, at least. Can you just tell me what it costs? I don't need the whole sales pitch.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Fair enough. We offer coverage anywhere from fifty thousand up to seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars, on either a ten- or twenty-year term. Given your daughter's age, a twenty-year term would take her to about twenty-four. Something like two hundred and fifty thousand would clear the line of credit and leave a decent cushion. I'll need to ask a few quick health questions to get you an actual price, though. There's no medical exam.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No needles? Good, I don't have time for that. Go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the last twelve months, have you used any tobacco or nicotine products, including vaping?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for heart disease, cancer, stroke, or diabetes?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, none of those.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Are you currently taking any prescription medication, or waiting on any tests or results?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Just an inhaler now and then for mild asthma. That's it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks. Mild asthma that's well controlled usually isn't a problem. Last one: have you been hospitalized overnight in the past five years?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Only when I had my daughter.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's fine. Based on those answers, two hundred and fifty thousand dollars over twenty years comes out to twenty-two dollars a month. That premium is fixed for the whole twenty years, so it won't go up.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Twenty-two bucks. Okay, that's less than I figured. What's the catch? Do I get anything back if I outlive it?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No, and I want to be upfront about that. This policy has no cash value. It's pure protection. If the term ends and you're still here, which is what we hope, the coverage just ends and there's no payout or refund of premiums.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hm. My accountant keeps going on about whole life policies that build up value. Should I be doing that instead?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Those exist, but they cost a lot more each month. For what you've described, covering the debt and your daughter while she's dependent, term usually fits well. But if you'd like to run it by your accountant first, that's completely fine. I can send you the quote and you can call back whenever suits you.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, I'd rather just get it done. I'll never find time to call back. But what if I change my mind next week?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: You've got a thirty-day free-look period. If you decide within thirty days that it's not for you, you can cancel and get a full refund of anything you've paid.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay, that helps. Should it be twenty years, or would ten be cheaper?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Ten would be a bit cheaper monthly, but it would end when your daughter's around fourteen, and getting new coverage at that point would be priced at your age then. Since you said you want her covered until she's out of school, twenty years lines up better. It's your call, though.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Twenty. Let's do twenty. Who gets the money, do I name someone now?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, we'll set up a beneficiary. Who would you like to name?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: My partner, Jordan Pelletier.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Got it, Jordan Pelletier as primary beneficiary. Before I finalize anything, let me summarize so we're on the same page. This is Acme Term Life, two hundred and fifty thousand dollars of coverage for a twenty-year term, at twenty-two dollars a month, fixed for the full term. There's no cash value, and you have thirty days to cancel for a full refund. Would you like to go ahead with that?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I want to go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. For the monthly payment, would you prefer a pre-authorized debit from a chequing account or a credit card?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Chequing's fine. I'll have to grab the void cheque info from my phone. Hang on.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. Transit 04512, institution 004, account 6627183.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, I've got that entered. Your first payment of twenty-two dollars will come out on the date the policy starts, and you'll get your policy documents by email within a couple of business days. The thirty days starts from when you receive them.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Perfect. Is that everything? I really need to get back.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's everything. Have a look over the documents when you get a chance, and call us if anything looks off. Thanks for your time, Ava, and good luck with the new space.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thanks, Ethan. Bye.
